name: Felixé Minas Haus Tannheim
kurzbeschreibung: The Felixé Minas Haus in Tannheim: a 300-year-old heritage town house showcasing authentic Baroque and Biedermeier living culture in the Tannheimer Tal.
beschreibung:
Overview

The historic Felixé Minas Haus is located in the picturesque village centre of Tannheim in the Tyrolean Tannheimer Tal (Reutte district) at Höf 43, at an altitude of around 1,097 metres. Nestled in the high alpine valley close to the border with the Bavarian Allgäu, this heritage-protected residence built around 1698 is among the most culturally significant and authentic bourgeois and farmhouse ensembles in Tyrol. As a fascinating cultural monument, the building provides a seamlessly preserved glimpse into the prosperity, artistic taste, and everyday life of an influential Tyrolean merchant and judicial family spanning three centuries.

Living Culture, Biedermeier & Architecture

The house owes its unusual name to its last private owner, Felix Rief, who in village custom was known simply as Felixé Mina after his father Felix ("Felixé") and his mother Mina. Following his death, the intact residence and its complete historic inventory passed into the ownership of the municipality and a foundation. The stately central-hallway house (Mittelflurhaus) combines the traditional timber block construction of the Außerfern with elements of aristocratic stone architecture. Stepping inside, visitors feel transported back in time: on display are original Swiss stone pine parlours from the Baroque and Biedermeier eras, magnificent tiled stoves made of Schongau faience, historic four-poster beds, intricately decorated chests, and a fully preserved family archive with deeds dating from the 17th century. A standout feature is the private house chapel boasting a Baroque altar and a papal mass licence granted in 1775. In the agricultural wing, historical implements illustrate alpine flax processing, sheep farming, and the supra-regional salt and flax trade that once brought considerable prosperity to the Tannheimer Tal.

Visit & Getting There

The Felixé Minas Haus is open to visitors during the summer season from early June to mid-October, and in the winter season from late December to late March, on Thursdays and Fridays from 14:00 to 17:00 (special guided tours for groups of 8 or more are possible year-round by advance telephone arrangement). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and youths (6 to 15 years) approx. €2.50, young children free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Holders of the Tannheimer Tal Sommer-Gästeticket receive discounted admission. Getting there by car: via the A7 motorway (exit Oy-Mittelberg) or via Reutte on the B199 (Tannheimer Straße) directly to Tannheim; parking is available at the municipal centre or at the Bergbahnen Tannheim. By public transport: train to Sonthofen (Germany) or Reutte in Tirol station, from where regional valley buses (line 120) run directly to the Tannheim Kreisverkehr / Gemeindeamt stop.

Tips

The ground floor of the historic house is accessible via a few steps; a historic wooden staircase leads to the upper parlours (not wheelchair accessible). Take time to listen to the knowledgeable cultural guides, who share vivid anecdotes about village life in centuries past. Combine your visit with a scenic walk to the nearby Vilsalpsee lake in the eponymous nature reserve.
oeffnungszeiten: Saisonal Do & Fr 14:00–17:00 Uhr (Gruppen auf Anfrage ganzjährig)
